scope_note: Very broad soil/sediment domain; clay, silt and sand cannot be treated as one universal PSD.
Preparation history changes fabric and coordination.
Includes nanometre clay pores, intergranular/dissolution bodies and MIP entry throats; method labels are essential.
Organic, clay and mineral pores dominate nano/submicron scales; cracks are separate.
Fractures control flow but must not be folded into matrix PSD.
Microporosity, interparticle and moldic systems coexist.
Vugs are bodies and do not imply equally large connecting throats.
Crack and equant-pore modes may coexist.
Large vesicles can remain poorly connected through small apertures.
Mostly grain-boundary/intragranular microcracks and cleavage porosity.
State-specific extension; not an intact-matrix reference.
Core-scale porosity is low; cracks/fractures can dominate transport.
Borehole log peaks and hydraulic permeability can be fracture dominated.
Intrinsic lizardite/brucite porosity is predominantly nanoscale; local interface porosity is not whole-rock porosity.
Bulk and transport porosity diverge strongly.
Not representative of coherent serpentinite matrix.
Protolith and fabric matter; matrix pores and grain-boundary cracks remain distinct.
